# Trefle API

> Trefle is an open REST API over a global plants database: the taxonomy from
> kingdom down to species, botanical traits (growth, flowers, fruits, edibility,
> soil, climate), geographic distribution zones, images and the sources every
> value comes from. This file is the short orientation for programs and AI
> agents; the complete, machine-readable contract is the OpenAPI document.

## Where things are

- Base URL: https://trefle.io/api/v1 (HTTPS only; JSON in and out)
- OpenAPI 3.0 document: https://trefle.io/api/v1/openapi.json (or .yaml), no token needed.
  It is generated from the API test suite, so it matches the running version
  (`info.version`). It lists every endpoint, the allowed filter/order/range
  keys per endpoint, the response schemas and the error envelope.
- Guides: https://docs.trefle.io (getting started, filtering, sorting,
  pagination, searching, client-side apps, data provenance)
- Rendered reference: https://docs.trefle.io/reference
- Source code and issue tracker: https://github.com/treflehq/trefle-api

## Authentication

Every endpoint needs an access token, except GET /api/v1 (public counters)
and the OpenAPI document. Create an account on https://trefle.io/users/sign_up
and copy the token from https://trefle.io/profile. Send it either way:

    Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN        (preferred)
    ?token=YOUR_TOKEN                        (query parameter)

A missing or invalid token answers 401. Never ship the account token in a
browser or mobile app: from your backend, claim a JWT bound to your origin
with POST https://trefle.io/api/auth/claim (JSON body
{"origin": "https://your.site", "ip": "optional client IP"}, authenticated
with the account token). It answers {"token": "<jwt>", "expiration": "..."};
the page then sends the JWT as its Bearer token. Read endpoints answer
cross-origin requests.

## Main endpoints

    GET /plants                      one record per plant (its main species), paginated
    GET /plants/{id}                 a plant with its main species and all its species
    GET /species                     every species, subspecies, variety, hybrid and cultivar
    GET /species/{id}                a species with its full trait data, images, sources, distribution, synonyms
    GET /plants/search?q=...         full-text search over plants (scientific name, common names, synonyms, author, family)
    GET /species/search?q=...        the same over species
    GET /species/{id}/facts          provenance: every sourced claim behind the species traits
    GET /genus, /genus/{id}, /genus/{id}/species, /genus/{id}/plants
    GET /families, /families/{id}, /families/{id}/genus
    GET /kingdoms, /subkingdoms, /divisions, /division_classes, /division_orders (and /{id})
    GET /distributions, /distributions/{id}, /distributions/{id}/species, /distributions/{id}/plants
                                     WGSRPD geographic zones (TDWG), by slug such as "fra" or "europe"
    GET /corrections, /corrections/{id}, /corrections/mine
    POST /corrections/{record_type}/{record_id}   submit a data correction (reviewed by hand)
    POST /species/{id}/report        report wrong data on a species, with a note
    GET /me                          the account the token belongs to

{id} is the numeric id or the slug (abies-alba). A synonym slug resolves to
the accepted species. Lists return a light version of each record; fetch
/species/{id} for the complete one.

## Response envelope

    Collection: {"data": [...], "links": {"self", "first", "prev", "next", "last"}, "meta": {"total": N}}
    Record:     {"data": {...}, "meta": {"last_modified": "..."}}
    Error:      {"error": true, "code": "not_found", "message": "...", "messages": "..."}

Error statuses: 400 (unknown filter/order/range key, invalid value, page too
deep), 401, 404, 422 (invalid body), 429 (rate limit), 500. `code` is a
stable machine-readable token; `messages` is a deprecated alias of `message`.

## Filtering, ranges and sorting

Bracketed object parameters, one key per field (OpenAPI style deepObject).
The allowed keys of each endpoint are in the OpenAPI document under
components.parameters (filter_species, range_species, order_species...); an
unknown key answers 400 with the list of valid keys.

    filter[field]=value          exact match; several values with commas match any of them:
                                 filter[flower_color]=red,pink
    filter_not[field]=null       exclude records where the field is empty (or equals the given values)
    range[field]=min,max         numeric range; leave max empty for an open range: range[maximum_height_cm]=1000,
    order[field]=asc|desc        sort; several order[...] keys sort on several fields

Boolean fields accept true, yes, 1, on, false, no, 0 and off.

Example, edible trees at least 10 m high, tallest first (curl needs -g, it
otherwise treats the brackets as globs):

    curl -g -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
      "https://trefle.io/api/v1/species?filter[edible]=true&filter[ligneous_type]=tree&range[maximum_height_cm]=1000,&order[maximum_height_cm]=desc"

Frequent species filter keys: common_name, scientific_name, family_name,
genus_name, rank, edible, edible_part, vegetable, duration, flower_color,
foliage_color, fruit_color, growth_habit, growth_form, growth_rate,
ligneous_type, leaf_retention, bloom_months, fruit_months. Frequent range
keys: year, average_height_cm, maximum_height_cm, light,
atmospheric_humidity, ground_humidity, ph_minimum, ph_maximum,
minimum_temperature_deg_c, maximum_temperature_deg_c, soil_texture,
soil_salinity, soil_nutriments, images_count, sources_count.

## Pagination

Collections return 20 items per page by default. per_page=N (1 to 100; limit=N
is an alias) sets the page size, page=N selects a page; prefer following
links.next. /species and /plants refuse page > 2500 (400): narrow the results
with filters or ranges instead.

## Rate limits and caching

60 requests a minute per IP and token by default (more for sponsors, see
https://trefle.io/about#support). Every response carries RateLimit-Limit,
RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset; a 429 adds Retry-After. Single
records answer ETag and Last-Modified, so conditional requests work.

## Licence and attribution

Data: CC BY 4.0 (https://trefle.io/terms). Cite Trefle and the sources each
species lists in its `sources`; see https://trefle.io/citation. Images keep
the licence of their source, given alongside each image. Trefle is open
source and non-profit; report wrong data through POST /species/{id}/report
or /corrections rather than silently correcting it downstream.
